claims.statement: Ashoka used inscriptions on rock and polished stone pillars to communicate beyond his court. They recorded royal instructions and ideas about conduct. The surviving inscriptions are evidence of particular statements in particular places, rather than proof that every subject lived by the same rules.

Ashoka’s rock and pillar inscriptions: 254 BCE to 232 BCE. Editorial window from the Met’s starting date of 254 BCE to the end of Ashoka’s reign. Not a continuous carving programme or the date of every edict.
